E-1   Fire

  • Call 911 immediately.** Give the address: **614 Western Avenue, Joliet.**
  1. Get everyone out of the house first — do not stop to collect belongings.
  2. Close doors behind you as you leave (slows fire spread).
  3. Meet at the **end of the driveway** so firefighters can account for everyone.
  4. Call 911 from outside or a neighbor's phone.
  5. Do not re-enter for any reason until fire department clears the building.
  • Fire extinguishers** are located at:
  • Under kitchen sink (right door)
  • Basement bar column (south wall)
  • Basement workshop
  • Attic stairway landing
  • Garage (wall-mounted)

Use an extinguisher only if the fire is small, contained, and you have a clear exit behind you. If in doubt, get out.

  • Do not** use water on a grease or electrical fire.
↑ top

E-2   Gas leak

If you smell gas: get out first, then call.

  1. Do not turn any light switches, appliances, or electronics on or off.
  2. Do not use your phone inside the house.
  3. Leave the door open as you exit — do not stop to close it.
  4. Once outside and away from the house, call **Nicor Gas: 888-642-6748.**
  5. Call 911 if the smell is strong or you feel dizzy.
  6. Do not re-enter until Nicor or the fire department gives the all-clear.

The gas meter and shutoff are located [RTN: verify location — likely on exterior south or west wall near the boiler vent]. Only Nicor should operate the main shutoff.

  • Do not** attempt to locate the leak yourself.
↑ top

E-3   Water / flooding

  • Main water shutoff: basement, northeast corner, near the water softener.** Turn the valve clockwise (right) to close.

If water is actively flowing and you cannot identify the source: 1. Shut off the main valve immediately. 2. Then identify the source.

  • Localized shutoffs** (for a single fixture without shutting off the whole house):
  • Every toilet has a shutoff valve at the wall behind the base.
  • Every sink has shutoff valves under the cabinet.
  • Washing machine has valves behind it on the wall.
  • Water heater has a valve on the cold-water inlet pipe above it.
  • Sump pump:** Located in the basement workshop, northeast corner. Note: the sump crock was sealed when the radon system was installed (2008) and has not been tested since. If basement flooding occurs, the sump pump may not function — call a plumber.

If flooding has reached electrical outlets or the electrical panel, do not enter the water. Call 911.

  • [RTN: verify basement valve map and any zone shutoff valves not listed here]**

E-4   Power failure

The house has a Generac 14kW standby generator that starts automatically within seconds of a grid outage. It runs on natural gas and requires no action from you.

  • What to expect:** 1. Lights go out briefly. 2. You may hear the generator start up in the backyard — this is normal. 3. Power restores to most of the house within 30–60 seconds.
  • If the generator does not start within 2 minutes:**
  • Check the generator status panel on the unit in the backyard.
  • Call Baker Electric: **815-942-3957.**
  • If you smell exhaust inside the house** after the generator starts, open windows and call Baker Electric. Do not run the generator with garage doors closed.
  • ComEd** (to report outage or check restoration status): **800-334-7661** or comed.com.

The generator runs a self-test every Saturday around 10 a.m. for about 5 minutes — this is normal and not an outage.

  • Note:** The landline telephone requires power to the modem. During an outage before the generator starts, use a cell phone.
↑ top

E-5   Tornado / severe weather

  • Shelter location: the root cellar / coal bin in the basement.**

The root cellar is in the northwest corner of the basement, behind the heavy wood door. It has thick limestone walls and a concrete ceiling — the safest place in the house.

  • When a tornado warning is issued for Joliet:** 1. Move to the basement immediately. Do not wait to see the storm. 2. Go to the root cellar and close the door. 3. Bring: cell phone, any medications needed, a flashlight. 4. Stay until the warning expires or an all-clear is issued.
  • Do not** shelter in the attic, near windows, or in the garage.
  • [RTN: confirm root cellar can be latched from inside; note anything stored there that should be cleared]**

E-7   Security / intruder

  • If you believe someone is in the house: leave if you safely can, then call 911.**

Do not confront an intruder. Get out through the nearest exit.

  • If you cannot leave safely:**

Two exterior doors have **double-cylinder deadbolts** (require a key from both sides). **[RTN: identify which doors have double-cylinder locks and where the interior key is kept — this is a fire-egress issue too.]**

E-8   No heat

First, check the obvious:

  1. **Check the thermostat** — is it set to Heat, and is the temperature set above the current room temperature?
  2. **Check the boiler** (basement utility room). Look at the pressure gauge — it should read between 12 and 25 psi. If the needle is in the red or at zero, do not attempt to adjust it yourself.
  3. **Check the circuit breaker** for the boiler — main panel in the basement workshop. The boiler breaker should be on.
  4. Look for a **reset button** on the boiler (typically a red button on the burner assembly). Press it once. Wait 2–3 minutes. If the burner lights and heat returns, you're done. Press reset only once — if it trips again, stop and call.
  • If none of the above resolves it:** Call **Johansen & Anderson: 815-723-9383.** Ask for the service department (Sharon or Michelle). They offer after-hours emergency service.
  • Note:** The boiler is 33 years old (installed 1993) and past its typical lifespan. If it fails and cannot be repaired promptly in cold weather, contact RTN immediately to discuss next steps.
  • In the meantime:** Electric space heaters can supplement heat. Do not use gas ranges or ovens for heating.
↑ top

E-9   No air conditioning

  1. **Check the thermostat** — is it set to Cool, and is the set temperature below the current room temperature?
  2. **Check the circuit breaker** for the AC — the Space Pak air handler is on the attic subpanel. The condenser (outdoor unit) is on the main panel in the basement workshop.
  3. **Check the filters** in the attic air handler. A clogged filter can cause the system to shut down. Filters are the two 16x20 panels in the air handler cabinet. If they are gray and matted, replace them (DuPont Ultimate 9600 Allergen, 16x20 — available at Menards or Home Depot).
  • If none of the above resolves it:** Call **Johansen & Anderson: 815-723-9383.** They service the Space Pak system under the annual contract.
  • In the meantime:** The **whole-house fan** in the attic can pull cool nighttime air through the house. Use it after dark when outside temperature drops below indoor temperature. Open at least one window before turning it on.
  • [RTN: confirm which breaker label covers the attic subpanel and outdoor condenser — add to SYS-1 Electrical when that section is written]**
↑ top

E-10   Radon alarm

The radon mitigation system has a red-liquid U-tube indicator visible in the basement. This shows whether the radon fan is running:

  • Left side lower than right side = fan is working correctly.** No action needed.
  • Both sides equal (fluid level) = fan has stopped.** The radon system is not functioning.
  • If the fan has stopped:** 1. Check the attic — the fan is mounted in the attic on the radon pipe. Listen for fan noise when near the attic access. 2. Check the attic subpanel for a tripped breaker. 3. If the breaker is on and the fan is not running, call **Timmit Radon Systems.** [RTN: phone number not yet recorded — look up current contact.]
  • While the fan is not running:**
  • Increase ventilation — open windows when weather permits.
  • Do not panic: radon levels rise slowly over days, not minutes.
  • Schedule a radon test after the system is repaired to confirm levels are back to normal.

The radon fan was last replaced July 31, 2018. Typical fan lifespan is 10 years — it is approaching the end of its expected life.

S-1   Fall (September–October)

Complete these tasks before the first freeze, typically by mid-October.

  • Air conditioning — shut down**
  1. Schedule the Johansen & Anderson fall visit (they will call to arrange it, but confirm if you haven't heard by September).
  2. Turn the AC thermostat to OFF or Heat mode.
  3. In the attic, remove the two 16x20 filters from the air handler. Wrap each in plastic and store them — they will be reinstalled in spring. (Filters are DuPont Ultimate 9600 Allergen, 16x20. Replace rather than rewrap if they are gray and matted.)
  4. Cap all 19 AC duct openings throughout the house with the plastic duct caps. Caps are stored in the root cellar at the west end.
  • Heating — start up**
  1. Bleed the radiators. Use the bleeding key kept in the tin can on top of the boiler. Open each radiator bleed valve briefly until water (not air) comes out, then close. Start on the top floor and work down.
  2. Check the boiler pressure gauge — it should read between 12 and 25 psi. If it reads outside that range, call Johansen & Anderson.
  3. Set the thermostat to Heat mode.
  • Exterior — winterize**
  1. Drain the garage faucet line to prevent freezing: - Close the feed valve to the right (north) of the basement powder room toilet (labeled). - Open the drain valve on the south wall of the powder room at floor level. - Open the exterior faucet on the north end of the east side of the garage, and the valve inside the garage in the same area. This allows air in and remaining water to drain back to the basement. - Leave the drain valve open all winter.
  2. The two house exterior faucets (east and west sides, midpoint) are frost-free and do not need to be drained.
  3. Store summer pond equipment (see S-4 / Pond section).
  • Pond — close**
  1. See SYS-11 Backyard Pond for the full pond closing procedure.
  • Schedule**
  1. Schedule the Johansen & Anderson boiler inspection (fall visit covers both AC and boiler).
  2. Order R.O. filter replacements from Osby Water Systems (219-996-4743) if not yet done this year.
↑ top

S-2   Winter (November–March)

  • Ongoing monitoring**
  • Check the boiler pressure gauge periodically — it should read 12–25 psi. A drop to zero means the system has lost water and needs attention. Call Johansen & Anderson.
  • Listen for the generator self-test every Saturday morning around 10 a.m. (runs about 5 minutes). If you do not hear it one Saturday, call Baker Electric: 815-942-3957.
  • Monitor the radon indicator tube in the basement. The left side of the U-tube should be lower than the right side. If levels are equal, the fan has stopped — see E-10.
  • Front step ice melter**

The front steps face north and are prone to ice. The electric heat cable embedded in the steps is controlled by a timer/breaker in the basement, east of the root cellar door (labeled, 40A dedicated circuit).

  • Set the timer appropriately for cold spells — do not run it continuously all winter.
  • Shovel snow first, then let the cable melt remaining ice. Do not rely on the cable as the sole ice removal method.
  • Turn the system off when freezing temperatures are no longer forecast.
  • Storm windows**

Storm windows should already be in place from fall. If any are loose or missing, address before the coldest weather arrives.

↑ top

S-3   Spring (April–May)

Complete these tasks once freezing temperatures are reliably past, typically by early May.

  • Air conditioning — start up**
  1. Schedule the Johansen & Anderson spring visit (they will call, but confirm if not heard from by April).
  2. Retrieve the stored 16x20 AC filters from wherever they were stored in fall. Unwrap and reinstall in the attic air handler. If they were wrapped in plastic and are still clean, they can be reused; replace if gray and matted.
  3. Remove all duct caps from the 19 AC duct openings throughout the house. Return caps to storage in the root cellar.
  4. Set the thermostat to Cool mode when ready.
  • Exterior — re-open**
  1. Re-open the garage faucet line: - Close the drain valve on the south wall of the basement powder room. - Open the feed valve to the right (north) of the toilet (labeled). - Check the exterior garage faucet and interior valve — confirm no leaks.
  • Pond — open**
  1. See SYS-11 Backyard Pond for the full pond opening procedure.
  • Drinking water filter**
  1. Call Osby Water Systems (219-996-4743) to order R.O. replacement filters if the system meter has shut the unit down (500-gallon limit reached). Filters are mailed to the house; replacement is a DIY job (see SYS-9).
  • IQAir filter (Bedroom 2)**
  1. Check the monitor light on the IQAir unit. If yellow or orange, order the indicated replacement filter from IQAir (877-715-4247, account 830881). They will mail it to the house.
↑ top

S-4   Summer (June–August)

  • Pond — ongoing**
  • Clean the pond skimmer filter every two weeks, or more often after storms or heavy wind.
  • Top off the pond water as needed — evaporation is significant in hot weather.
  • See SYS-11 for full pond operating procedures.
  • Whole house fan**

The whole house fan in the attic is most useful in summer. On hot days that cool off at night, use it after dark to flush hot indoor air and pull in cool outside air.

  • Open at least one window before turning the fan on.
  • Open the attic door on the second floor (required for airflow).
  • Operate with the remote (kept in kitchen or master bedroom).
  • Do not run the fan during rain or if outdoor air is more humid than indoor air.
  • Storm windows and screens**
  • Remove storm windows from rooms that will use screens during summer. Store storms safely — they are fragile and expensive to replace.
  • Screens are available for 19 windows. Commonly used: east windows in Bedrooms 1 and 2, east and south windows in Bedroom 3, screen insert in Bedroom 4 door, two casement and sash windows in the kitchen east wall.
  • Music room casement windows keep their storms year-round.
  • Back porch screens stay year-round (no storm windows for that area).
  • AC monitoring**
  • Check the AC filters in the attic handler mid-summer. If they are heavily loaded, replace rather than wait for fall.
  • If rooms are not cooling evenly, check that all 19 duct caps are removed and ducts are open.

SYS-1   Electrical

The house has three electrical panels.

  • Main panel** — basement workshop, east wall near the north end. A breaker list is posted on the wall to its right. This is the primary panel for the house and garage.
  • Attic subpanel** — south portion of the attic, ceiling-mounted. Fed by Breaker 19 (20A) in the main panel. Contains four 15-amp sub-breakers (labeled A through D). Powers attic lights, outlets, radon fan, whole-house fan, and the bathroom on the second floor (partial).
  • Garage subpanel** — garage, east wall. Fed by Breaker 10 in the main panel. Two sub-breakers:
  • Sub-breaker 1: garage door opener and exterior motion detector lights. Controlled by a wall switch in the kitchen to the right of the back porch door (labeled). Switching this off disables the garage opener from the house.
  • Sub-breaker 2: all other interior garage lights.
  • Exterior electrical outlets:**
  • Front porch: 15A
  • Rear deck: northeast outlet 20A, southeast outlet 15A
  • Garage northeast corner: 15A
  • If a breaker trips:** Reset by switching it fully off, then back on. If it trips again immediately, do not reset a third time — call an electrician.
  • [RTN: add full breaker list for main panel as a table in a future session]**

SYS-3   Boiler & radiators

The house is heated by a Weil-McLain gas boiler (175,000 BTU, installed ca. 1993) feeding cast iron radiators throughout. Hot water is circulated by a pump; the radiators warm by radiation and convection — no forced air.

  • Normal operation:** Set the thermostat to Heat. The boiler fires automatically to maintain the set temperature. You should hear the burner ignite and the circulator pump run.
  • Boiler power switch:** On the left (north) side of the boiler. The toggle should point **down** for power ON.
  • Pressure gauge:** Should read 12–25 psi during normal operation. Check it occasionally.
  • Below 12: system may need water added — call Johansen & Anderson.
  • At zero: system has lost pressure — call Johansen & Anderson.
  • In the red zone: call Johansen & Anderson immediately.
  • Fill valve and pressure reducer:** Overhead to the left of the water softener. Do not adjust without guidance.
  • Reset button:** A red button on the burner assembly. If the boiler has locked out (no heat, burner not firing), press the reset button once and wait 2–3 minutes. If it trips again, stop and call Johansen & Anderson — do not press reset more than once.
  • Bleeding radiators** (done each fall before heating season): 1. Get the bleeding key from the tin can on top of the boiler. 2. Starting on the top floor, open each radiator bleed valve (small square valve on one end of each radiator) a quarter turn. 3. When water — not air — flows out steadily, close the valve. 4. Work your way down floor by floor.
  • Service:** Johansen & Anderson (815-723-9383) hold the annual service contract. They inspect and service the boiler each fall. Call them for any breakdown.
  • Note:** The boiler was manufactured in 1991 and installed ca. 1993 — it is well past its typical 25-year lifespan. It continues to operate but should be on the watch list for replacement planning.

SYS-4   Air conditioning (Space Pak)

The house uses a Space Pak high-velocity system — designed for older homes without standard ductwork. Air is distributed through 19 two-inch ducts throughout the first and second floors.

  • Air handler:** Located in the attic. Contains two 16x20 filters.
  • Condenser:** Outdoor unit, east side of the house near the generator.
  • Filters:** Two 16x20 DuPont Ultimate 9600 Allergen filters. Replace each spring; wrap in plastic and store each fall. Available at Menards and Home Depot. If they are gray and matted, replace rather than reuse.
  • Duct caps:** 19 plastic caps, one per duct opening. Stored in the root cellar (west end) during cooling season. Cap all ducts each fall when AC shuts down; remove all caps each spring.
  • If the AC is not cooling:** 1. Check thermostat — set to Cool, set temperature below room temperature. 2. Check filters — a clogged filter causes the system to shut down. 3. Check breakers — attic subpanel (air handler) and main panel (condenser). 4. Call Johansen & Anderson (815-723-9383) if none of the above resolves it.
  • Service:** Johansen & Anderson inspect and service the system each spring under the annual contract.

SYS-5   Standby generator

The house has a Generac 14kW standby generator (model G0072230, serial 3008453556) installed June 2021, located east of the house next to the AC condenser.

  • Fuel:** Natural gas — no refueling required.
  • Auto-start:** The generator starts automatically within seconds of a grid power failure. Power restores to most of the house within 30–60 seconds. No action needed from you.
  • Self-test:** Every Saturday morning at approximately 10 a.m., the generator runs for about 5 minutes. This is normal — not an outage. You will hear it running.
  • Capacity:** 14kW — sufficient to power everything normally run simultaneously in the house.
  • Monitoring:** Baker Electric (815-942-3957) monitors the generator remotely via the internet and performs annual maintenance including oil changes. Fee approximately $250/year.
  • Warranty:** Expires June 23, 2028. Covers parts, labor, and travel for Baker Electric and other authorized service personnel.
  • If the generator does not start during an outage:**
  • Check the status panel on the generator unit.
  • Call Baker Electric: 815-942-3957.
  • If you smell exhaust inside the house:** Open windows immediately and call Baker Electric. Never run the generator with the garage door closed.
  • ComEd** (grid power outage reporting): 800-334-7661 or comed.com.

SYS-8   Internet & phone

  • Service:** AT&T fiber optic internet and landline telephone.
  • Modem/router:** Located in the south closet of the music/guest room. The closet also holds the master cordless telephone base and the computer/music equipment rack.
  • Wi-Fi:** Two access points cover the house. **[RTN: note access point locations and network name for manual]**
  • Landline telephone:** The landline runs through the AT&T fiber modem. It requires power to the modem to function. During a power outage — in the brief window before the generator starts — the landline will be dead. Use a cell phone.
  • If internet is down:** 1. Check the modem/router in the music room closet — indicator lights should be on. 2. Restart the modem: unplug power, wait 30 seconds, plug back in. Allow 2 minutes to reconnect. 3. If still down, call AT&T.

SYS-9   Water softener & R.O. filter

  • Water softener (Kenmore):** Located in the basement near the main shutoff.
  • Check salt level every 2–3 months. Keep at level 4–5 (not full to the brim).
  • Use standard water softener salt pellets.
  • The fill valve and pressure reducer for the radiator network are overhead to the left of the softener — do not confuse with the softener controls.
  • Reverse osmosis filter (Kinetico):** Located in the basement workshop, west wall. Feeds the drinking water faucet at the kitchen sink (separate faucet in right corner of right basin). Also feeds the refrigerator ice maker.
  • The system filters to near-distilled quality.
  • A meter shuts the system off after 500 gallons. At that point, order replacement filters from Osby Water Systems (219-996-4743) — they have the account on file and know which filters are needed. Filters are mailed to the house.
  • When fully charged, the system can dispense about two quarts before needing 1–2 hours to recharge.
  • Keep spare filters near the tank.
  • R.O. filter replacement procedure:** 1. Obtain two filters (a MAC and a C-1) from Osby Water Systems (219-996-4743). 2. On the right blue canister, move the small brass lever on top toward you one quarter turn to close. 3. Lift the holding tank off its platform (it is heavy). At the top inside the black ring cap, turn the white prongs clockwise to close the shutoff valve. 4. Press the small red air pressure release button on top of the right blue canister. 5. Using the R.O. wrench, loosen the right blue canister counterclockwise (viewed from the bottom), then unscrew by hand. It will be full of water. 6. Remove the used C-1 filter. Pour out remaining water. Sanitize: add one teaspoon of bleach, fill with fresh water, let stand 5 minutes, empty. Rinse and wipe dry. 7. Install the new C-1 filter. Replace and hand-tighten the canister. 8. Repeat steps 5–7 for the left blue canister, replacing the MAC filter. 9. Open the holding tank valve: turn white prongs counterclockwise until they stop. Return the tank to its platform. 10. Open the right canister valve: move the brass lever to the right until parallel to the wall. 11. Open the filtered water tap at the kitchen sink for 2 minutes to purge air and carbon dust. 12. The system will take about an hour to fully recharge.

Detailed instructions are also posted on the wall to the right of the storage tank in the basement workshop.

SYS-11   Backyard pond

The pond is seasonal — open spring through fall, drained for winter. There are no fish.

  • Spring opening:** 1. Retrieve pond equipment from the root cellar (paraphernalia stored there over winter). 2. Inspect the pond for debris accumulated over winter — clean as needed. 3. Reinstall the pump and skimmer. 4. Fill the pond with water. 5. Start the pump and confirm water is circulating.
  • Weekly maintenance (in season):**
  • Clean the skimmer filter every two weeks, or after storms.
  • Top off water level as needed — evaporation is significant in hot weather.
  • Check pump operation — if water is not circulating, check for clogs.
  • Fall closing:** 1. Remove the pump from the water and bring it inside for winter — do not leave it in the pond. 2. Drain the pond: use the large drain valve at floor level south of the basement powder room toilet (behind the green-hosed drain valve). Leave this valve open all winter. 3. Clean out leaves and debris before fully draining. 4. Store all pond equipment (pump, hoses, accessories) in the root cellar for winter.

R-2   Living room & library

  • Fireplace:** **Do not burn wood.** The fireplace has a gas line running up from the basement through the ash chute, feeding a gas-fired coal set. The coal set has a pilot light that should stay lit year-round.

To use the fireplace: 1. Fully open the flue: turn the knob above the fireplace on the left side counterclockwise as far as it will go. 2. Use the remote to start the fire. 3. Glass doors can be open or closed. If closed, remove the small ash pit door in the basement (grab the two handles and pull gently) — this allows combustion air to flow up from the basement. Reinsert the door when finished. 4. To extinguish: use the remote. Reinsert the ash pit door. Close the flue.

The fireplace is decorative — not a practical heat source. Never leave it on unattended or overnight.

  • Display lights:**
  • Two wall picture lights (east of front door; west wall over sofa) — permanently mounted, run on timers plugged into wall outlets.
  • Sculpture light in the library area west of the front door — low voltage, mounted in a ceiling beam. Timer and transformer are in the cavity behind the small door on the right (north) side of the attic stairway, about five steps up. To disable, unplug the transformer.

R-8   Basement

The basement has four rooms plus a powder room.

  • Main room** (beneath the original house): The largest space, containing a wet bar with hot and cold water and a double sink. Previously divided by a partition (removed to open the space). Contains:
  • Freezer: Kenmore, model 253.22442412, serial WB60947989. Placed in service March 8, 2016.
  • Refrigerator: Kenmore, model 461.62402. Placed in service October 2010.
  • Microwave: Kenmore, model 721.62222300, serial 307TA00102. Placed in service ca. late 2003.
  • Washer: Kenmore, model 110.92588210, serial CE2512674. Placed in service July 1995.
  • Dryer: Kenmore, model 110.97588210, serial ME2605182. Placed in service July 1995. Clean lint trap every use; vent duct annually.
  • Water softener (Kenmore) — see SYS-9.
  • Boiler (Weil-McLain, 175,000 BTU) — see SYS-3.
  • Water heater (Kenmore gas, 40 gal, installed February 28, 2017).
  • Storage room** (north of staircase, 8.5 × 11 ft, lockable door): General storage. Has been used as a sleeping room in a pinch.
  • Workshop** (beneath the kitchen): Contains the main electrical panel, the sump pump (sealed 2008, likely non-functional — see E-3), and the reverse osmosis filter on the west wall.
  • Root cellar / coal bin** (beneath the front porch): Originally used for coal storage. Now long-term storage and **tornado shelter** — surrounded by heavy limestone foundation walls and a 7-inch poured concrete porch deck overhead. Glass block windows on two sides with small screened openings for ventilation. Screen rack for 19 windows stored at the west end. Pond equipment stored here over winter. AC duct caps stored here during cooling season.
  • Powder room:** Toilet and wash basin. Closet contains the central vacuum unit. Most of the plumbing shutoff valves for the house are overhead in this room — all labeled.
↑ top

R-9   Attic

  • Access:** Door on the second floor hallway.
  • Solar roof ventilation fan:** Mounted on the south face of the hip roof (installed June 2018). Thermostatic — turns on above 80°F when the solar plate is lit, off below 70°F. No routine maintenance required.
  • Insulation:** Two-inch foil-coated polyisocyanurate panels fastened to the underside of the roof deck joists. Separates the joist cavities from the rest of the attic so the solar fan only exhausts joist cavity air. Eight one-square-foot eave holes (two per side) allow fresh air in.
  • Whole house fan:** Located below the panel insulation. Exhausts household air into the joist cavity and out through the solar fan's exhaust port. Automatic doors open when the fan is on, close when off. Two remotes — one in the kitchen, one in the master bedroom. **Requires:** attic door open and at least one window open on first or second floor before operating.
  • Plumbing rough-in:** Hot and cold capped feed stubs protrude from the attic floor near the vent stack for the bathrooms below — installed for any future owner wishing to add a bathroom.
  • Subpanel:** South portion of the attic (ceiling-mounted). Four 15A sub-breakers. Fed by Main Panel Breaker 19 (20A). Powers attic lights, radon fan, whole-house fan outlets, and partial second floor bathroom circuits.
  • Circuit 19 (20A)** powers the subpanel and the outlets on the east side of the north dormer (radon fan, whole-house fan). Circuit 14 (15A) powers attic overhead lights and the outlet behind the small panel door in the first attic stair run. Circuit 15 (15A) powers the south dormer east outlet (TV antenna amplifier).

REF-6   House history

614 Western Avenue was built around 1910. The foundation and exterior walls are Joliet limestone — the distinctive yellowish-gray stone quarried locally that gives the house its character and places it within Joliet's architectural heritage.

The house was purchased by the Nachtrieb family in 1995.

The original draft of this manual (Volume I) was written by Robert Nachtrieb beginning around 2021–2022. A planned Volume II was to document the house's history in detail, including a landmark nomination, chronology of prior owners, oral history interviews, and requirements for external modifications visible from the street. That volume was not completed.
